endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Root cause analysis should examine upstream human-factor contributors (e.g., insufficient onboarding, role-skill mismatch, production pressures that discourage critical review).

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether community town halls or listening sessions surface concerns about higher-risk AI before or during deployment, and no study documents the hazard itself. The single endorsing source, a CHAI governance playbook, is quoted on root cause analysis of human-factor contributors and does not speak directly to community listening sessions.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The one endorsement comes from a framework, and its quoted text addresses root cause analysis rather than community engagement, so it offers indirect support at most.

Because no study was supplied, there is no information on whether listening sessions reach Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy communities. Any claim that town halls capture the concerns of these groups currently rests on assumption rather than data.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare organizations holding community town halls or listening sessions on higher-risk AI with those that do not. Useful outcomes include the number and type of concerns raised before deployment, changes made to deployment plans in response, attendance by demographic group, and later measures of patient trust or complaints. No such study appears in the supplied evidence.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of the practice exists, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. This means organizations cannot assume that listening sessions reach these groups, and those that adopt the practice may need to track who attends and who does not.
